payload.rationale: M is calibrated Elo->1x2 (predict_1x2, neutral symmetrized) at d_eff=+273. Spain is Elo #1 and the process backs the rating: a World-Cup-record 6 consecutive clean sheets (EARNED, not variance) - lowest xGA of any remaining team (~0.85), opponent xG under 1.0 every match, Unai Simon 519 min without conceding - with a functional-not-explosive attack (won R16 1-0 late over Portugal, 1.74-0.72 xG). Belgium (Elo #13, aging) is result-flattered and volatile: out-xG'd by Senegal 3.18-1.84 in the R32 (one-way traffic for 86 min, survived on keeper/xGOT), then genuinely dominant vs USA (2.15-0.67) but the 4-1 margin inflated by clinical finishing (De Ketelaere, Lukaku super-sub); Belgium concedes quality chances, Spain does not. Expert consensus + Opta (Spain ~13% tournament / 3rd, Belgium ~2%) all favor Spain. M: Spain 70.4%, draw 19.1%, Belgium 10.5%. J = M: no market-unavailable information. The process edge (Belgium worse than its record) points toward Spain but is market-known (sharp books use xG) and pushing J higher would run into the documented 'Elo overconfidence on big favorites' tail (pilot +6.5~24pp, m95 Argentina +12.8pp); pushing J lower would require the forbidden 'Elo overrates favorites' input (m91/Rui-Alg lesson). So J=M, committed as a scorable datapoint carrying the big-favorite overconfidence risk transparently.
invalidation: Confirmed pre-match XI shows Spain resting/missing multiple core starters (Yamal / Pedri / Rodri) -> amend toward Belgium.
Yamal's earlier hamstring flares and he is out or clearly limited -> amend toward Belgium.
Belgium confirmed to field De Bruyne + Lukaku + Doku all from the start AND at full fitness (a materially stronger XI than the one that beat USA) -> small amend toward Belgium.
Confirmed Spain missing a first-choice CB (Laporte/Cubarsi) with a clear downgrade -> small amend toward Belgium.
Extreme weather / major disruption -> note but do not repredict.

basis: J = M by deliberate discipline. Consulted the full evidence pack (Opta tournament-win, Nate Silver co-favorite, both teams' full xG/process, injuries/fitness, unanimous expert previews favoring Spain).

No LEGITIMATE market-unavailable information found to move J off M: all injuries/fitness (KDB not match-fit, Lukaku managed, Nico Williams out), Belgium's fatigue, Spain's venue familiarity, and both teams' underlying xG are public and priced by sharp books.

The process asymmetry (Spain's earned elite defense vs Belgium's finishing-inflated, out-xG'd run) is real and points toward Spain, but it is MARKET-KNOWN (xG is public) -> not a J-vs-market edge. Pushing J higher than M's 70.4% would drive deeper into the documented 'Elo/Poisson overconfidence on big favorites' tail (pilot +6.5~24pp, m95 Argentina +12.8pp), which is precisely the failure mode this experiment tracks.

Rejected input (doctrine): 'Elo overrates a +267 favorite, so shade J down toward the market.' This is the forbidden 'Elo-vs-market known divergence' mechanism; it would make J a market simulator (m91/Rui-Alg lesson). Explanation-only: it predicts the market may price Spain BELOW M's 70.4%, but J does not move on it.

Expected M/J-vs-market posture: most likely the market prices Spain somewhat below 70.4% (the big-favorite tail) -> any Spain-side gap is my model's overconfidence bias, not a market error -> Pass per m95 discipline. On Belgium, M is already at only 10.5% (likely at or below market) so no fade-Belgium edge either. Committed to J=M as a real, scorable data point.
